name: Cauliflower
climate: Cool-season; best in cool to mild conditions
tip: Avoid growth checks from drought or heat while heads are forming.

name: Cabbage
tip: Use insect netting early to reduce caterpillar damage.

name: Brussels Sprouts
climate: Cool-season; long cool growing period preferred
tip: Firm soil around plants and harvest sprouts progressively from the lower stem.

name: Kale
climate: Cool to mild; tolerates light frost
tip: Harvest outer leaves first so the centre keeps producing.

name: Silverbeet
climate: Most Australian climates outside extreme heat
tip: Pick outer stalks regularly to extend production.

name: Celery
tip: Celery dislikes drying out; mulch well and maintain steady moisture.

name: Leek
depth: Seed 5–10 mm; transplant into 10–15 cm holes
tip: Earth up gradually or use deep transplant holes for longer white stems.

name: Spring Onion
tip: Succession sow small batches every few weeks for continuous harvests.

name: Parsnip
tip: Use fresh seed and keep the seedbed moist because germination can be slow.

name: Turnip
tip: Harvest roots young for the best texture; leaves are also edible.

name: Swede
tip: Best root quality develops during cool weather with steady growth.

name: Sweet Potato
climate: Warm-season; subtropical, tropical and warm temperate
tip: Do not overfeed with nitrogen or vines may grow at the expense of tubers.

name: Eggplant
tip: Wait for warm soil before planting outside and harvest fruit while glossy.

name: Chilli
climate: Warm-season; subtropical and tropical plants may perennialise
tip: Warm soil improves germination; protect seedlings from cold nights.

name: Okra
climate: Hot warm-season; subtropical to tropical and warm summers elsewhere
tip: Pick pods young and frequently before they become tough.

name: Asparagus
depth: Crowns in 15–20 cm trench, gradually backfill
harvest: Light harvest after 2 years; full harvest from year 3
climate: Temperate to subtropical with suitable dormancy
tip: Allow fern growth after harvest season to recharge the crowns.

name: Artichoke
depth: Seed 1 cm; plants at nursery level
tip: Give plants plenty of room and harvest buds before scales open.

name: Broad Bean
tip: Support tall plants and pinch tops after pod set if aphids gather there.

name: Snow Pea
tip: Provide a trellis at sowing and pick pods frequently while flat and tender.

name: Rocket
climate: Cool to mild; grows much of the year in many regions
tip: Harvest young leaves and succession sow to avoid tough, overly peppery growth.

name: Bok Choy
tip: Fast uninterrupted growth helps prevent premature bolting.

name: Pak Choy
tip: Use insect netting where caterpillars and flea beetles are troublesome.

name: Kohlrabi
tip: Harvest swollen stems before they become large and woody.

name: Fennel
climate: Cool to mild; avoid peak heat for bulb fennel
tip: Keep bulb fennel growing steadily; transplant gently because root disturbance can trigger bolting.

name: Endive
tip: Cool weather gives the best leaf quality and reduces bitterness.

name: Mustard Greens
tip: Harvest young leaves for milder flavour and sow successive batches.

name: Rhubarb
depth: Crown buds at or just above soil level
harvest: Light harvest after first year; established plants thereafter
climate: Cool to temperate; needs winter chill for best dormancy
tip: Only eat the stalks; rhubarb leaves contain high oxalate levels and should not be eaten.

name: Basil
tip: Pinch growing tips and flowers regularly to encourage leafy branching.

name: Parsley
tip: Germination can take several weeks; keep seed consistently moist.

name: Coriander
sun: Full sun in cool weather; part shade in warmth
tip: Sow small batches frequently because heat quickly triggers flowering.

name: Mint
harvest: Leaves within 6–10 weeks from established divisions
climate: Most Australian climates with adequate moisture
tip: Grow in a container if you need to prevent aggressive spreading.

name: Rosemary
climate: Temperate, Mediterranean and many subtropical gardens
tip: Excellent drainage is more important than frequent watering.

name: Thyme
harvest: 10–14 weeks from seed; sooner from divisions
climate: Temperate to subtropical with good drainage
tip: Trim lightly after flowering to keep plants compact and productive.

name: Oregano
tip: Flavour is strongest in sunny conditions without excessive fertiliser.

name: Sage
harvest: 12–16 weeks from seed; light harvest sooner from established plants
tip: Prune lightly after flowering and replace old woody plants when productivity declines.

name: Dill
harvest: 6–10 weeks for leaves; seed heads later
tip: Direct sow because dill dislikes transplanting; succession sow for continuous leaves.

name: Chives
tip: Cut leaves near the base and divide crowded clumps every few years.

name: Tarragon
propagation: Division or cuttings for French tarragon
climate: Cool to temperate; winter dormant in colder areas
tip: French tarragon rarely produces useful seed, so buy plants or propagate vegetatively.

name: Lemongrass
climate: Warm temperate to tropical; frost sensitive
tip: Harvest outer stems at ground level and leave the centre to regrow.

name: Bay Laurel
tip: Container growing is useful where you want to control the mature size.

name: Marjoram
climate: Temperate to subtropical; protect from severe frost
tip: Frequent light harvesting encourages bushy new growth.
